item.text:
<linkedin_post>A list of possible terms can help a speech model handle unfamiliar vocabulary, provided the instruction tells it to use those terms only when the audio supports them. For a medical recording, that might mean supplying spellings such as “HbA1c” and “metformin” along with the desired language and transcript format.

NVIDIA recommends trying this kind of context with Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe before fine-tuning. Its medical speech case study then goes further: training examples include near-miss terms so the model learns to distinguish a useful spelling hint from a word that was never spoken.

Even with a domain-specific prompt, names and technical terms need checks against the recording. A plausible term in the context list can be a costly substitution if it changes the meaning of a medical discussion.</linkedin_post>
